summary: Iteration 44 — Flutter back bug fix verified end-to-end. Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass (demo block lists are clean, Frank→Joyce + Joyce→Frank reply works with correct wording, the originally-broken Frank↔Margaret round-trip now returns 200, explicit /users/{id}/block still enforces 403 with 'Cannot flutter this user'). Frontend: logged in as Frank via demo, the seeded Margaret flutter rendered with the new 'sent you a flutter 🦋 — reply with a flutter or start a chat' wording, tapping 'Flutter back' showed the success toast 'Flutter sent to Margaret 🦋' and removed the row (no generic 'Couldn't send flutter' error). Chat button navigates to /dm/<conversation>. BrandLockup + Today's Thought + greeting render correctly in the expected order. No regressions detected.
critical_code_review_comments: send_flutter() correctly returns 403 only when sender is in receiver.blocked — the bug was data, not logic. Demo seed/migration fix was the right call.
flutterBack() error handler in home.tsx now disambiguates the 403 'Cannot flutter' branch from rate-limit, 404, and generic errors. Wording is friendly and non-judgemental.

Reply detection in send_flutter (line 7187) uses find_one on flutters in the reverse direction — works correctly for the Joyce→Frank reply path. Verified message comes back as 'replied with a flutter 🦋 — would you like to start a chat?'.

Minor: there is still no public /unblock endpoint. The block test had to clean up via direct Mongo $pull. Consider adding POST /api/users/{user_id}/unblock/{other_id} for completeness, but not blocking.
seed_data_creation: Seeded one flutter Margaret→Frank via POST /api/flutters/send for the UI test. The test then consumed it via the 'Flutter back' tap; resulting Frank→Margaret flutter remains in the demo dataset (harmless benign demo data). Explicit-block regression test added a temporary block from Bill→Dorothy and removed it via direct Mongo $pull in a try/finally so demo state is restored.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Demo block lists are confirmed empty for all 8 demo accounts as of this iteration. The flutter back round-trip works for any demo pair. If a future test seeds flutters between demo accounts and re-runs reply-detection tests, remember to db.flutters.delete_many() the prior history first — reply wording vs opening wording depends on whether any prior flutter exists in the reverse direction. Rate limit is 20/hr per sender (HTTP 429), so heavy back-to-back testing should rotate sender accounts.
